title: Trunk Based Development
summary: Trunk-based development: everyone commits to one branch at least daily, with short-lived branches, feature flags and a build server; claimed to avoid merge hell and enable continuous delivery.

assertions.quote: This ensures the codebase is always releasable on demand and helps to make Continuous Delivery a reality.
Shared branches off mainline/main/trunk are bad at any release cadence
Trunk-Based Development is a key enabler of Continuous Integration and by extension Continuous Delivery.
short-lived feature branches are used for code-review and build checking (CI), but not artifact creation or publication

verdicts.note: Branch lifetime, not branch existence, drives integration pain; this is the consensus position in continuous delivery literature.

DORA characterises effective trunk-based development as fewer than three active branches and branches or forks living less than a day before merging to master, so short-lived branches merged within a day count as trunk-based in its predictive model.

assertions.quote: techniques should include feature flags, branch by abstraction and "don't break the build"
Development teams can casually flex up or down in size (in the trunk) without affecting throughput or quality.

verdicts.note: Google's monorepo shows it is possible with heavy tooling investment; Brooks's-law effects do not vanish because of a branching model.

assertions.quote: you are going to need to hook up a build server to verify that their commits have not broken the build

verdicts.note: CI servers are near-universal practice; the threshold is a rule of thumb.
